minor: "Its renewal rate stayed at 92.9 percent, which showed members still trusted the price": the source gives 92.9% only for fiscal 2024, so "stayed" is not backed for 2022-23, and "showed members still trusted the price" is an inference. Say "was 92.9 percent in fiscal 2024" and soften the claim.
"where many retailers take far more" has no listed source; the cited NYT piece supports only the roughly 14 percent cap.

"selling bulk goods to members who paid a fee": early Price Club was aimed mainly at small businesses, with individual members added later. "Members" is acceptable, but "small-business members" would be more exact.
"Since 2006 the basic fee has risen four times, from $45 to $65": the first rise ($45 to $50) happened in 2006 itself, so "since 2006" is slightly loose. "Starting in 2006" fits better.
"made in plants it set up itself" goes slightly beyond the 2009 reporting, which says "its own plants". Use the source's wording.
The cold open calls Sinegal "its co-founder" and the body calls him "a founder" and "the founder"; use "co-founder" consistently.

"Sinegal's answer, as Jelinek later told it" is fine, but the Jelinek exchange and the Sinegal quote are both Jelinek's undated account. The script already says so mid-video; consider saying it before the first quote.
